source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 page/heap-row layout, TOAST, and pg_attribute documentation; SQLite file-format and datatype documentation; MySQL 8.4 InnoDB row-format and type-storage documentation; and the cited Ramakrishnan/Gehrke and Garcia-Molina/Ullman/Widom storage foundations. All seven online official destinations returned HTTP 200. Vendor-specific header, null, alignment, serial-type, hidden-field, and overflow claims are explicitly scoped by engine and version.

evidence: Checked H, N, bitmap bytes B, aligned data start D, attribute alignments a_i, starts o_i, stored lengths s_i, exclusive ends e_i, and tuple size T.
Checked that logical length, stored inline length, overflow referenced length, padding, record boundary, and page boundary remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The recurrence describes only the labeled pedagogical format and is not presented as a vendor ABI or file format.

evidence: Recomputed one bitmap byte and the 32-byte aligned data start from a 24-byte header and two nullable attributes.
Recomputed field starts 32,36,40,48,60 and stored sizes 4,1,8,9,16.
Recomputed logical value bytes 158, overflow tuple bytes 80, null-case tuple bytes 64, and all-inline tuple bytes 208.
Recomputed simplified 8168-byte page density as 97 records at 84 bytes including slot and 38 records at 212 bytes including slot.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Capacity calculations are explicitly bounded estimates and not measurements of PostgreSQL, SQLite, or InnoDB.

evidence: Re-derived bitmap bytes as ceil(N/8), aligned data start, per-field alignment, exclusive ends, and final record alignment.

evidence: Reviewed zero nullable fields, bitmap byte boundaries, all-null/all-present rows, empty versus null values, maximum alignment, padding, and exact record end.
